findings.current: the lingering heat of the battlefield seemed to freeze
findings.defect: The source states that the lingering heat froze; “seemed to” adds uncertainty that is not present.
findings.rationale: The Korean says the battlefield’s remaining heat 얼어붙었고—froze—without a hedge.
findings.replacement: the lingering heat of the battlefield froze in an instant

findings.current: The three old fiends from Tianshan
findings.defect: “Fiends” adds a judgment of wickedness not established by the source’s “three old men.”
findings.rationale: The Korean calls them 천산의 세 늙은이, literally the three old men of Tianshan; the source does not call them fiends.
findings.replacement: The three old men from Tianshan

findings.current: a man Hyeoncheon would gladly tear to pieces
findings.defect: This loses the source’s emphasis that tearing the enemy’s bloodline apart and killing him would still not satisfy Hyeoncheon.
findings.rationale: 단숨에 찢어 죽여도 시원치 않을 conveys that even tearing and killing the enemy at once would not be enough to satisfy him.
findings.replacement: the bloodline of an enemy he could tear apart and kill in an instant and still not feel satisfied

summary: The translation is largely faithful, with a few small shifts in certainty, characterization, and emphasis.
